title: CPSC, Suzuki Announce Recall of Automatic Transmission Eiger ATVs
reason: Suzuki Motor Corporation has determined that the Eiger automatic ATVs were produced with an internal manufacturing flaw. This flaw could cause the crankshaft to break during operation. A broken crankshaft will interrupt power transfer from the engine to the transmission and the drive wheels, leaving the driver stranded away from his or her base of operation.
firm: American Suzuki Motor Corporation, of Brea, Calif.
distribution: Suzuki dealers nationwide sold these ATVs, from September through mid-October 2001, for between $4,400 and $5,200.
hazards: Suzuki Motor Corporation has determined that the Eiger automatic ATVs were produced with an internal manufacturing flaw. This flaw could cause the crankshaft to break during operation. A broken crankshaft will interrupt power transfer from the engine to the transmission and the drive wheels, leaving the driver stranded away from his or her base of operation.
remedies: Consumers should contact their local Suzuki dealer to schedule an appointment for their ATV to be inspected and repaired. Suzuki will replace all Eiger ATVs for a new one if the unit is brought in by January 31, 2002. After that date, they will be offering a free inspection and repair. American Suzuki Motor Corporation will notify consumers directly about this recall.
injuries: There have been four incidents, in which the crankshaft broke during operation. No accidents or injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Lite Machines Corp. Announce Recall of Motor Speed Controller
product: Fusion 35 speed controllers (shipped with Corona electric helicopter kits)
reason: The Fusion 35 motor speed controller may not operate properly, due to a weakness in a batch of integrated circuit (IC) chips. The (IC) chip can become hot and damage the controller. In certain instances, a malfunctioning IC chip can cause the helicopter motor to turn on for the several seconds before the power is disconnected, which can damage the helicopter or cause injury to the operator or bystanders.
firm: Lite Machines Corporation, of West Lafayette, Ind.
distribution: These components were sold with the electric helicopter kits at hobby shops, from November 2001 through December 2001, for about $60.
hazards: The Fusion 35 motor speed controller may not operate properly, due to a weakness in a batch of integrated circuit (IC) chips. The (IC) chip can become hot and damage the controller. In certain instances, a malfunctioning IC chip can cause the helicopter motor to turn on for the several seconds before the power is disconnected, which can damage the helicopter or cause injury to the operator or bystanders.
remedies: Consumers should send the Fusion 35 speed controller to Lite Machines for a diagnostic test by the manufacturer. If the unit is defective, it will be replaced free of charge.
injuries: There were three incidents where the motor came on for several seconds and damaged the helicopter. There have been no injuries.

title: CPSC, Kawasaki Motor Corporation Announce Recall of ATVs
reason: The rear wheel hubs, in the case of the KLF220 and KLF300-B, and the front and rear wheel hubs of the KLF300-C, are held to their respective axles by a castellated nut, that is secured to the axle with a specified torque, then locked in place by a cotter pin. On a limited number of the affected models, the axle nut was not tightened to the proper torque before the cotter pin was inserted. The cotter pin or axle nut failure could cause the hub to come off of the axle shaft, creating the potential for an incident, resulting in injury or death to the rider.
firm: Kawasaki Motors Corp., U.S.A. (KMC), of Irvine, Calif.
distribution: Kawasaki dealers sold these ATVs nationwide in November 2001, for between $3,000 and $5,000.
hazards: The rear wheel hubs, in the case of the KLF220 and KLF300-B, and the front and rear wheel hubs of the KLF300-C, are held to their respective axles by a castellated nut, that is secured to the axle with a specified torque, then locked in place by a cotter pin. On a limited number of the affected models, the axle nut was not tightened to the proper torque before the cotter pin was inserted. The cotter pin or axle nut failure could cause the hub to come off of the axle shaft, creating the potential for an incident, resulting in injury or death to the rider.
remedies: Consumers should contact their Kawasaki dealer to schedule an appointment. The dealer will apply the correct torque to the axle nut. Kawasaki Motor Corporation has notified consumers directly about this recall.

title: CPSC and TruHeat Corp. Announce Recall of Spa Heaters

reason: The spa heaters have an internal electrical connection that can overheat and ignite the heater and spa, posing a fire hazard.
distribution: Independent spa dealers nationwide sold spas with these heaters from January 1997 through January 2001. The price for these spas is between $4,000 and $9,000.
hazards: The spa heaters have an internal electrical connection that can overheat and ignite the heater and spa, posing a fire hazard.

The hinges also must minimize any spaces that could allow a child's finger to be pinched, crushed or lacerated.
remedies: Consumers should stop children from using these toy boxes immediately, and contact Palliser for a free replacement toy box or a $50 refund.

title: CPSC, Milwaukee Electric Tool Corp. Announce Recall of Electric Wrenches
reason: The wrenches have power cords that can release from the handle, posing an injury or electrocution hazard to consumers.
firm: Milwaukee Electric Tool Corp., of Brookfield, Wis.
distribution: Home centers, hardware stores, and industrial distributors nationwide sold these wrenches, from March 2001 to July 2001, for between $180 and $280.
hazards: The wrenches have power cords that can release from the handle, posing an injury or electrocution hazard to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these electric wrenches immediately and return them to the nearest Milwaukee Factory Service Center or authorized power tool service center for a free repair. Wrenches that have a "X" stamped or etched on the nameplate next to the serial number have already been repaired.
injuries: Milwaukee and CPSC have not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Warn Industries Inc. Announce Recall of ATV Winch Kits
product: Winch Kits used with All-Terrain Vehicles (ATVs)
reason: An electrical component of the winch kit, the solenoid, poses a fire hazard when used in this application, even when the vehicle is parked and the winch is not in use.
firm: White-Rodgers
distribution: ATV dealers and specialty retailers nationwide and mail order catalogs sold these ATV winch kits, from November 2000 through May 2001, for about $400.
hazards: An electrical component of the winch kit, the solenoid, poses a fire hazard when used in this application, even when the vehicle is parked and the winch is not in use.
remedies: Consumers should immediately disconnect the solenoid wires from their ATV and call their local ATV dealer or Warn Industries to receive the free replacement solenoid and installation instructions.
injuries: Warn Industries has received five reports of ATV fires started from winch kits installed on these vehicles in the U.S., and four reports of ATV fires in Canada. One consumer reportedly suffered smoke inhalation as a result of one of these fires. The fires resulted in loss or damage to the ATVs and, in some cases, adjacent vehicles or surrounding structures.

title: CPSC, Basic Comfort Inc. Announce Recall of Infant Seat Pads
reason: The seat pad has two shoulder straps that create a v-shaped opening around the head and neck, presenting a strangulation hazard to young children.
distribution: Basic Comfort Inc., of Denver, Colo.; Department and juvenile products stores nationwide including JC Penney and One Step Ahead sold these infant seat pads, from October 1998 through May 2001, for about $11.
hazards: The seat pad has two shoulder straps that create a v-shaped opening around the head and neck, presenting a strangulation hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the infant pads immediately and contact Basic Comfort to receive a replacement.
injuries: Basic Comfort received one report of an 8-month old girl who was caught by the neck in the shoulder straps of the seat pad after falling sideways off a chair. The child was removed from the seat pad without injury.

title: CPSC, NIKE USA Inc. Announce Recall of Jordan Trunner Cross-Training Shoes
reason: The shoes have a thin metal strip on the outside of the heel that can protrude from the shoe and form a sharp edge that can cut consumers.
firm: NIKE USA Inc., of Beaverton, Ore.
distribution: Major athletic shoe and department stores nationwide sold these shoes, from July 1999 through July 2001, for between $90 and $125.
hazards: The shoes have a thin metal strip on the outside of the heel that can protrude from the shoe and form a sharp edge that can cut consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these cross-training shoes immediately and contact NIKE to receive free replacement shoes.
injuries: NIKE has received six reports of the metal strip protruding from the Bubble, including five cuts to the lower leg that required stitches; one injury report on the Trunner; and no injury reports on the Trunner Mid or Trunner 2000. The Trunner Mid and 2000 models are included in the recall to prevent the possibility of injury.

title: CPSC, Inca Imports Announce Recall of Stuffed Bears
reason: The noses, bells, and eyes of the bears can detach, presenting a choking hazard to young children. The eyes also present a sharp point hazard.
distribution: Stores in tourist areas throughout Arizona, California, Colorado, Montana, Nebraska, Oklahoma, and Texas sold the bears, from July 1997 through February 2001, for between $20 to $50.
hazards: The noses, bells, and eyes of the bears can detach, presenting a choking hazard to young children. The eyes also present a sharp point hazard.
remedies: Consumers should take these stuffed bears away from young children immediately and return them to the store where they were purchased, for a full refund.
injuries: CPSC and Inca Imports have not received any reports of injuries. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, The Toro Company Announce Recall of Riding Mowers
product: Toro and Exmark brand commercial duty zero-turn radius riding mowers
reason: Spilled fuel can ignite during refueling, when fuel vapors are drawn into the hot muffler.
firm: The Toro Company, of Bloomington, Minn.
distribution: Toro and Exmark commercial dealers sold these riding mowers nationwide, between January 1998 and March 2001, for between $6300 to $11,200.
hazards: Spilled fuel can ignite during refueling, when fuel vapors are drawn into the hot muffler.
remedies: Call Exmark or Toro to determine if the riding mower is part of the recall. If so, local Exmark or Toro dealers will install a spark arrester and (selected Exmark models only) a new fuel tank for free. Registered owners should already have been contacted by letter.
injuries: Toro has received 28 reports of fires and 12 reports of minor burn injuries, mainly to commercial users.

title: CPSC, Firms Announce Recall of Hand Trucks, Baby Walkers
product: P-Handle Hand Trucks and Baby Walkers
reason: If the tires of the hand trucks are substantially over-inflated beyond the recommended maximum 30 P.S.I., the rims of the tire can separate under the intense pressure and strike the user or bystanders. The walkers will fit through a standard doorway and are not designed to stop at the edge of a step. Babies using these walkers could be seriously injured or killed if they fall down stairs.
distribution: Sears stores exclusively sold these P-Handle hand trucks, from February 2001 through May 2001, for about $30. Independent discount stores located in California, Arizona and Texas sold these baby walkers, from January 1998 through July 2001, for between $18 and $22.
hazards: If the tires of the hand trucks are substantially over-inflated beyond the recommended maximum 30 P.S.I., the rims of the tire can separate under the intense pressure and strike the user or bystanders. The walkers will fit through a standard doorway and are not designed to stop at the edge of a step. Babies using these walkers could be seriously injured or killed if they fall down stairs.
remedies: Consumers should contact UnionTools, Inc. to receive a free repair kit. Consumers should only use a hand pump to inflate the tires. Consumers should stop using these baby walkers immediately and call SunTome Trading Corp. for instructions on returning the walkers for a refund and shipping costs.
injuries: UnionTools has received two reports of the tire rims separating due to over inflation of tires. Two adult males received serious hand lacerations and bruises as a result of the tire rims blowing apart. None reported involving the baby walkers.

title: CPSC, JT USA Inc. Announce Recall of Proteus Paint Ball Masks
reason: The plastic facemask could crack around the ear cover, when hit by a paint ball. This could allow the facemask to come off, exposing consumers to eye injuries.
firm: JT USA Inc., of Chula Vista, Calif.
distribution: Paintball equipment stores sold these masks nationwide, from March 2001 through May 2001, for between $110 and $150.
hazards: The plastic facemask could crack around the ear cover, when hit by a paint ball. This could allow the facemask to come off, exposing consumers to eye injuries.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these masks immediately, and return them to JT USA for a free replacement mask.
injuries: JT USA has received one report of a mask breaking around the ear cover. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Krups Announce Recall of Coffeemakers
reason: An electrical connection in these coffeemakers can overheat and ignite the filter basket support, presenting a risk of fire and burn hazard to consumers.
firm: Krups North America, of Closter, N.J.
distribution: Department, appliance and specialty stores nationwide sold the coffeemakers, from January 1996 through April 2000, for about $95.
hazards: An electrical connection in these coffeemakers can overheat and ignite the filter basket support, presenting a risk of fire and burn hazard to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should unplug and stop using the coffeemakers immediately and contact Krups North America, to receive a free replacement coffeemaker.
injuries: Krups has received 37 reports of the coffeemakers overheating, including 12 reports of fire and smoke damage to cabinets, countertops and surrounding objects. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Atico International USA Inc. Announce Recall of Percolators
reason: If the thermostat fails, the plastic housing of the percolator can overheat and melt while in use, posing a fire hazard.
firm: Atico International USA Inc., of Fort Lauderdale, Fla.
distribution: Drug and discount stores nationwide sold these percolators, from January 1996 through January 2001, for about $10.
hazards: If the thermostat fails, the plastic housing of the percolator can overheat and melt while in use, posing a fire hazard.
remedies: Firm no longer in business. Recall remedy no longer available. Discard the product. Do not donate or resell.
injuries: Atico has received six reports of fires, as a result of overheating with these percolators, resulting in minor property damage to kitchen counters and cabinets. There have been two reports of minor burns to the hand.

title: CPSC, Raymond Geddes & Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Velcro Wallets
reason: The zipper pull in the wallet contains lead, which can present a risk of lead poisoning to young children.
distribution: Toy stores nationwide sold these wallets, from August 1998 through April 2001, for about $1.
hazards: The zipper pull in the wallet contains lead, which can present a risk of lead poisoning to young children.
remedies: Consumers should immediately take these wallets away from children, and return the wallets to the store where purchased, for a refund.
injuries: CPSC and Raymond Geddes & Co. Inc. have not received reports of any injuries relating to these wallets. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

title: CPSC, Peg Perego USA Announce Recall of High Chairs
reason: When the seat is reclined, the high chairs have a space between the armrest and backrest, in which a child's head or arm can become entrapped. This can pose a risk of suffocation or injury to the heads or arms of young children.
distribution: Chain stores and independent retailers, including Babies "R" Us, Right Start, and Burlington Coat Factory, sold these high chairs, from June 1996 through October 1999, for about $180.
hazards: When the seat is reclined, the high chairs have a space between the armrest and backrest, in which a child's head or arm can become entrapped. This can pose a risk of suffocation or injury to the heads or arms of young children.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the high chairs immediately. Consumers should call Peg Perego to receive free replacement armrests that will eliminate the entrapment hazard. Consumers should not return the high chair to the store where purchased.
injuries: Peg Perego and CPSC have received 51 reports of entrapment, when children placed their heads or arms in the space between the armrest and backrest. Two children suffered scratches to the head, one had a bruised arm, and another had a scratched arm. There have not been any reports of suffocation.

title: CPSC, Imperial Toy Corp. Announce Recall of Toy Feeding Sets
product: CUDDLES FEEDING SET or "CUDDLES MEAL TIME" toy feeding sets
reason: The nipple on the toy baby bottle included in these sets could come off, posing a serious choking hazard to small children.
firm: Imperial Toy Corp., of Los Angeles, Calif.
distribution: Ben Franklin, Revco and other discount stores nationwide sold the toys, from October 1995 through May 2001, for about $2.
hazards: The nipple on the toy baby bottle included in these sets could come off, posing a serious choking hazard to small children.
remedies: Consumers should take these recalled toys away from young children immediately, and return the toy set to the store where purchased, for a refund.
injuries: CPSC and Imperial Toy Corp. are not aware of any incidents or injuries involving these toys. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury or death.

title: CPSC, DSI Toys, Inc. Announce Recall of Toy Kittens
product: Kitty Kitty Kittens stuffed toy kittens
reason: These toys contain contaminated water that, if contacted, could cause illness to children.
distribution: Discount, specialty, and toy stores nationwide sold the kitten toys from September 2000 through May 2001 for between $10 and $13.
hazards: These toys contain contaminated water that, if contacted, could cause illness to children.
remedies: Parents and caregivers should take these kitten toys away from children immediately, and discard or destroy them. The firm is out of business, so a replacement toy is no longer available.
injuries: CPSC and DSI Toys had not received any reports of illness resulting from contacting contaminated water from these toys. This voluntary recall was conducted as a precaution.

title: CPSC, Advantage Publishers Group Announce Recall to Replace Educational Kits
product: Let's Start™ Numbers and "Optical Illusions Lab" educational kits
reason: The red painted numbers on the acetate stencil sheet included in the "Let's Start™" kit contain lead; and the gold paint bearing the words "Kasy's Extrafine" on the black pen included in the "Optical Illusions" kit has lead.
firm: Advantage Publishers Group, of San Diego, Calif.
distribution: Retail stores, national book chains, wholesalers and distributors, and membership warehouse clubs nationwide sold the educational kits, from February 1999 through May 2001, for between $13 and $20.
hazards: The red painted numbers on the acetate stencil sheet included in the "Let's Start™" kit contain lead; and the gold paint bearing the words "Kasy's Extrafine" on the black pen included in the "Optical Illusions" kit has lead.
remedies: Consumers should immediately remove the stencil sheets and pens from the activity kits and discard them. Customers should call Advantage Publishers Group to order a replacement piece.
injuries: CPSC and Advantage Publishers Group have not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries. Lead poisoning is a serious hazard to children, and is associated with behavioral problems, learning disabilities, hearing problems and growth retardation.

title: CPSC Announces Recall of Furnaces in California
product: Gas-fired horizontal furnaces commonly called NOx rod furnaces
reason: These furnaces pose a substantial risk of fire.
firm: Consolidated Industries (formerly Premier Furnace Co.)
distribution: Home, hardware and specialty stores, and independent contractors sold these furnaces in California, from January 1983 through December 1992, for about $2,000.
hazards: These furnaces pose a substantial risk of fire.
remedies: This recall remedy is no longer available. The firm that announced the recall is out of business.
injuries: CPSC has received 50 reports of fires associated with the 140,000 horizontal furnaces manufactured by Consolidated Industries Inc. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Apple Announces Recall of AC Adapter for Prior Generation PowerBook Laptops
reason: These AC adapters could overheat, posing a fire hazard.
firm: Apple, of Cupertino, Calif.
distribution: Electronic and computer stores worldwide and Apple's website sold these AC adapters with PowerBook G3s, from May 1998 through March 2000. They also were sold separately for about $69.
hazards: These AC adapters could overheat, posing a fire hazard.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these AC adapters and contact Apple to receive a free replacement.
injuries: Apple received six reports of these adapters overheating. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Neiman Marcus Announce Recall of Plantation Furniture, Antique Mirror
product: Twin plantation bed headboards, queen plantation bed headboards, plantation nightstands and antique tin mirrors
reason: The furniture could be painted with lead-containing paint. Ingestion of lead from deteriorating paint is a major source of lead poisoning for children 6 years old and under.
firm: Neiman Marcus, of Chesnut Hill, Mass.
distribution: The furniture was sold through Neiman Marcus and Horchow catalogues from May 1998 through May 2001.
hazards: The furniture could be painted with lead-containing paint. Ingestion of lead from deteriorating paint is a major source of lead poisoning for children 6 years old and under.
remedies: Consumers should call Neiman Marcus to arrange for free pick-up and a full refund.
injuries: No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Cans Unlimited, Inc. Announce Recall of Kerosene Heaters/ Cookers
product: Fujika Models KSP-229 and KSP-231 Hi-Pet Heaters/Cookers
reason: The recalled units are not approved for use indoors. Use indoors can lead to injury and possibly death from carbon monoxide poisoning. The cookers also do not have an automatic extinguishing mechanism that would operate if they turned over, and lack adequate guarding.
firm: Cans Unlimited Inc. (CUI), of Greer, S.C.
distribution: Cans Unlimited, Inc. catalog and web site sold these units nationwide, between April 1999 and January 2000, for $63 to $93.
hazards: The recalled units are not approved for use indoors. Use indoors can lead to injury and possibly death from carbon monoxide poisoning. The cookers also do not have an automatic extinguishing mechanism that would operate if they turned over, and lack adequate guarding.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled kerosene heater/cooker immediately and contact Cans Unlimited, Inc. to receive a refund or replacement. Purchasers were sent direct mail notification of this recall.

title: CPSC, The Flood Co. Announce Recall of Wood Strippers and Cleaners
reason: Some of these bottles can leak at the cap, allowing the contents to come into contact with consumers. These strippers and cleaners can cause burns to the skin and eyes.
firm: The Flood Co., of Hudson, Ohio
distribution: Paint and hardware stores nationwide sold these Flood products, from March 2001 through June 2001, for between $15 and $20.
hazards: Some of these bottles can leak at the cap, allowing the contents to come into contact with consumers. These strippers and cleaners can cause burns to the skin and eyes.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled cleaners immediately, since the bottles can leak, and call the Flood Co. hotline. The hotline will help consumers determine if their bottle is leaking, and provide instructions on how to dispose of leaking bottles and get a refund.
injuries: The Flood Co. has received two reports of bottles leaking that were shipped to retailers, but no injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Hallmark Creations Announce Recall of Tea Light Lamps
reason: The plastic shade that covers the tea light candle can melt, posing a fire hazard.
distribution: Hallmark Creations stores nationwide sold these lamps, from January 2001 through May 2001, for about $12.
hazards: The plastic shade that covers the tea light candle can melt, posing a fire hazard.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the lamps immediately and return them to a Hallmark Creations store for a refund.
injuries: Hallmark has received three reports of the lampshade melting. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Chicco USA Inc. Announce Recall of Preschool Toys
reason: Some of the larger-sized ball halves can become stuck on a young child's face, covering the nose and mouth, and causing suffocation.
distribution: Amazon.com, Army & Air Force Exchanges and other toy stores nationwide sold these toys, from January 1999 through April 2001, for about $6.
hazards: Some of the larger-sized ball halves can become stuck on a young child's face, covering the nose and mouth, and causing suffocation.
remedies: Parents and caregivers should take these balls away from young children immediately and return the toys to the store where purchased for a refund.
injuries: CPSC received a report of a 2-year-old boy who had a ball-half stuck on his face, covering his nose and mouth. A nearby adult was able to pull the toy from his face. No injury to the child was reported.

title: CPSC, Five Firms Announce Recall of Backpack Blowers
reason: The fuel tanks on these blowers can leak, posing a fire hazard and risk of burn injuries to consumers.
firm: Husqvarna Forest & Garden Co., of Charlotte, N.C.; John Deere Consumer Products Inc., of Moline, Ill.; Makita U.S.A. Inc., of La Mirada, Calif.; Carswell Import & Marketing Associates Inc., of Winston-Salem, N.C.; Tilton Equipment Co., of Rye, N.H.
distribution: Home centers, hardware stores and manufacturer dealers nationwide sold these blowers for between $400 and $750.
hazards: The fuel tanks on these blowers can leak, posing a fire hazard and risk of burn injuries to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled blowers immediately, and contact the manufacturer to have their blower repaired free of charge.
injuries: Carswell has received 159 reports of leaking fuel tanks on these blowers. Makita U.S.A has received 55 reports of leaks. John Deere has received five reports of leaks. No injuries have been reported. The other firms have not had reports of leaks.

title: CPSC, Firms Announce Recall of Chain Saws and Child Table Seats
product: Chain Saws and Child Table Seats
reason: A missing screw can cause the chain brake to fail to operate, presenting a laceration hazard to consumers. The seats were sold without a seat belt, posing a risk to children who climb out of the seat.
firm: Stihl Inc., of Virginia Beach, Va.; Inglesina USA Inc., of Montclair, N.J.
distribution: Stihl dealers sold the chain saws, from December 2000 through May 5, 2001, for about $270. Department stores and toy stores sold the Table Chair from June 2000 through May 2001 for about $50.
hazards: A missing screw can cause the chain brake to fail to operate, presenting a laceration hazard to consumers. The seats were sold without a seat belt, posing a risk to children who climb out of the seat.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled chain saw immediately and return it to the Stihl dealer where purchased for repair. Consumers should immediately stop using the seats and call Inglesina USA to receive a replacement or a full refund.
injuries: Stihl Inc. had none reported. Inglesina USA has received one report of a 10-month-old girl who fell from a table seat, and bruised her back.

title: CPSC, Fluke Corp. Announce Recall of Electrical Testers
product: Fluke T-2 hand-held electrical voltage and continuity testers
reason: The recalled units can "lock-up" and stop working. When the tester "locks-up" it stops working for approximately 8 minutes without warning. Consumers testing electrical sources could fail to be warned of the presence of live current if the tester is not properly operating, posing a risk of shock, electrocution, and thermal burns.
firm: Fluke Corp., of Everett, Wash.
distribution: Home centers, hardware stores and industrial distributors nationwide sold these testers, between June 1999 and March 2001, for about $49.
hazards: The recalled units can "lock-up" and stop working. When the tester "locks-up" it stops working for approximately 8 minutes without warning. Consumers testing electrical sources could fail to be warned of the presence of live current if the tester is not properly operating, posing a risk of shock, electrocution, and thermal burns.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these voltage and continuity testers immediately, and contact Fluke for information on returning the recalled unit to Fluke for a free repair. Fluke has sent direct notice to known purchasers.
injuries: Fluke has received one report of a tester that "locked-up" and stopped working. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Firms Announce Recall of Remote Controlled Toy Race Cars and Galileo Weather Thermometers
product: Remote Controlled Toy Race Cars and Galileo Weather Thermometers
reason: Problems with the circuits are rendering some of the Remote Controlled Race Cars inoperable. These cars can overheat and emit smoke and may pose a potential burn hazard. The thermometers contain a liquid that is flammable and a hazardous substance that could be harmful or fatal if swallowed.
distribution: Participating Texaco gas stations nationwide sold the cars under the "Need for Speed" promotion, from May 2001 through June 1, 2001, for about $12, with any $10 purchase.; The Christmas Tree Shops Inc. in Massachusetts, Maine, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Connecticut, and Albany, New York sold these thermometers, from June 2000 through December 2000, for $12.99.
hazards: Problems with the circuits are rendering some of the Remote Controlled Race Cars inoperable. These cars can overheat and emit smoke and may pose a potential burn hazard. The thermometers contain a liquid that is flammable and a hazardous substance that could be harmful or fatal if swallowed.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these cars immediately, remove the batteries from the remote controlled race cars and the remote controls and return the remote controlled race cars and remote controls to the Texaco station where purchased, for a full refund. Consumers also may return the items for a full refund, by obtaining a prepaid shipping label by calling Equity Marketing Inc. Consumers should stop using these thermometers immediately and return them to the Christmas Tree Shops Inc. where purchased, for a refund.
injuries: Equity Marketing Inc. has received three reports of the toy cars emitting smoke. No injuries have been reported.

CPSC and Nantucket Distributing Co. Inc. have received five reports of thermometers breaking resulting in two injuries. A man suffered burns to his hands when the thermometer broke near a stove and ignited his clothing. Another man suffered smoke inhalation when extinguishing a fire caused by candles igniting a broken thermometer.

title: CPSC, KB Toys Announce Recall of Activity Gym Toys
product: Electronic Light N' Learn activity gyms
reason: Five detachable hanging rattle toys have small round pegs at the top of the toys that can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
distribution: KB Toy store, KB Toy Works, KB Toy Outlet, Big Lots, Odd Lots, Pic N Save and MacFrugals nationwide sold the toys, from September 2000 through January 2001, for between $20 and $30. The toys also were sold online at KBKids.com.
hazards: Five detachable hanging rattle toys have small round pegs at the top of the toys that can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately and return the toy to the store where purchased for a refund. Consumers who purchased the toy online, should return the toy to the closest KB Toy store or contact KB Toys for return information.
injuries: CPSC and KB Toys have received six reports of the pegs breaking off, including two reports of a 6- month-old-boy and a 14-month-old-boy beginning to choke off of a broken piece of the rattle attachment.

title: CPSC, Century Announce Recall of Multi-Use Strollers
reason: The strollers can unexpectedly collapse or the car seat/carrier adapter can unexpectedly detach. When this happens, an infant or young child inside the stroller or an attached car seat/carrier can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries.
firm: Century Products Co., of Macedonia, Ohio
distribution: Mass merchandise, juvenile products and discount department stores nationwide sold these strollers, from approximately December 1996 through March 2001, for between $100 and $200.
hazards: The strollers can unexpectedly collapse or the car seat/carrier adapter can unexpectedly detach. When this happens, an infant or young child inside the stroller or an attached car seat/carrier can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these strollers and call Graco to order a free repair kit. Consumers should have their strollers available, as Graco will help consumers determine if they have one of the recalled models.
injuries: Century has received 681 reports of incidents, including 250 injuries when the stroller unexpectedly collapsed or the car seat/carrier adapter detached. These reports include three concussions, two skull fractures, one fractured elbow, and two chipped teeth. The remaining injuries include bruises and cuts.

title: CPSC, Gymboree Announce Recall of Baby Boy Bodysuits
reason: The wheel-shaped zipper pull can twist off and become a choking hazard to young children.
distribution: The Gymboree website and stores nationwide sold these bodysuits, from March 2001 through May 2001, for about $17.
hazards: The wheel-shaped zipper pull can twist off and become a choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these outfits and return them to any Gymboree store for a full refund.
injuries: CPSC and Gymboree have not received any reports of injuries. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

title: CPSC, BRIO® Announce Recall of Toy Baking Sets
reason: The sets include a hand mixer with a knob that can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
distribution: Specialty stores, Internet retailers, and mail order catalogs sold the toys nationwide, from March 1999 through April 2001, for $15 to $25.
hazards: The sets include a hand mixer with a knob that can break off, posing a choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should take the hand mixer away from children immediately and call BRIO for a refund or replacement item. Consumers also can send the mixer to BRIO Corp., SAFETY RECALL, N120 W18485 Freistadt Road, Germantown, WI 53022, for a refund or replacement.
injuries: CPSC and BRIO have not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Battat Incorporated Announce Recall of Beanbag Cushions Suffocation and Strangulation Hazards to Babies Cited
product: Parents™ magazine-brand Soft Landing Beanbag cushions
reason: This product is an infant cushion manufactured by Battat for Parents™ magazine. In addition, two 8- to 9-inch cords, which attach toys to the cushions, pose strangulation hazards.
firm: Battat Incorporated, of Plattsburgh, N.Y.
distribution: Target stores nationwide sold the cushions, from September 2000 through May 2001, for about $24.
hazards: This product is an infant cushion manufactured by Battat for Parents™ magazine. Infant pillows and cushions have been banned under the Federal Hazardous Substances Act since 1992 because they pose a suffocation hazard to infants. In addition, two 8- to 9-inch cords, which attach toys to the cushions, pose strangulation hazards.
remedies: Consumers should take the cushions away from children immediately and return the cushions to a Target store for a refund. Consumers also can send their cushions to Battat Incorporated, Attention: Valinda Cayetano, Quality Assurance, 44 Martina Circle, Plattsburgh, NY 12901 for a refund plus mailing costs.
injuries: Battat has received one report of the cord attached to the rattle on one of these cushions becoming wrapped around the neck of a 7-month-old baby boy, causing red marks.

title: CPSC, Hedstrom® Corp. Announce Recall of Swings on Backyard Gym Sets
product: Star Cruiser® and Rocket Rider® swings on backyard gym sets
reason: Screws that hold the swing together can fall out, causing the seat to fall to the ground, posing an injury risk to children.
distribution: Department, toy, discount, lumber, and hardware stores nationwide, including Toys "R" Us, Wal-Mart and Kmart, sold the gyms, from September 2000 through April 2001, for $150 to $400.
hazards: Screws that hold the swing together can fall out, causing the seat to fall to the ground, posing an injury risk to children.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the swings immediately, detach them from the gym set, and discard or destroy them. The firm is out of business and a repair is no longer available.
injuries: Hedstrom had received 291 reports of seats separating, including 19 children who suffered lacerations, scrapes and bruises.

title: CPSC, Saks Incorporated Announce Recall of Boys' Vests
